quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #24
										  					
  

36 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: On roadways, bicycles are considered:

options.text: Hazards.
Vehicles.
Dangerous.

questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles on roadways. Cyclists and drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians are walking along the road ahead.
A pedestrian crossing is ahead.
Pedestrians cannot cross here.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells drivers that pedestrians may be crossing. If a pedestrian is in the crosswalk, you must stop and stay stopped until they finish crossing.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road changes direction or gets narrower.
No right turn.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road changes direction or gets narrower.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a change in direction or a narrower road ahead. You may see this sign on sharp curves or near narrow bridges.

questions.question: You see oncoming vehicles on your left and parked vehicles on your right. How should you steer?

options.text: Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.
Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.
Down the middle between both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Down the middle between both sides.
questions.explanation: When oncoming vehicles are on your left and parked vehicles are on your right, steer down the middle between them.

questions.question: Which lane should you be in to turn left from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane closest to the left side.
The lane closest to the center.
The lane closest to the right side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left side.
questions.explanation: Turn from the lane closest to where you want to go. For a left turn on a one-way street, use the lane closest to the left side.

questions.question: This sign shows one type of:

options.text: Intersection.
Road curve.
Right turn.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that another road crosses the highway ahead.

questions.question: Never make a U-turn:

options.text: in residential areas.
at or on a railroad crossing.
where there is no "No U-turn" sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: at or on a railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: Never make a U-turn at or on a railroad crossing. Also avoid U-turns where signs forbid them, on divided highways, when you cannot see 200 feet in each direction, on one-way streets, or in front of fire stations.

questions.question: If convicted of driving with a high blood alcohol level, you may go to jail for:

options.text: Up to six months.
Up to 12 months.
No jail time, but a $500 fine.

questions.explanation: For a first DUI conviction with a high blood alcohol level, you may spend up to six months in jail and pay a fine of $390 to $1,000. Your car may also be impounded.

questions.question: Which road is most likely to be slippery after snow or rain in cold weather?

options.text: A hilly, open road
A residential road
A road in a shaded area

questions.correctAnswerText: A road in a shaded area
questions.explanation: Shaded areas on roads freeze before other parts and thaw later. They are most likely to be icy in cold, wet weather.

questions.question: You are on a one-way street. You can turn left onto another one-way street only if:

options.text: You speed up before the turn.
Traffic moves to the right.
Traffic moves to the left.

questions.explanation: You can turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves left, if no sign prohibits it. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves right.

questions.question: You drive defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car in front of you.
Keep your eyes moving to spot possible hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your eyes moving to spot possible hazards.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means scanning the road ahead for hazards. Staring only at the road directly in front of you is dangerous. Check around you constantly for threats.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No turning.
No left turn.

questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around at this location.

questions.question: It is illegal to park your vehicle:

options.text: In an unmarked crosswalk.
Within three feet of a private driveway.
In a bicycle lane.

questions.explanation: You cannot park in a marked or unmarked crosswalk. You can park in a bicycle lane if there is no "No parking" sign and your car does not block cyclists.

questions.question: When should you give up your right-of-way?

options.text: Often, even at controlled intersections.
Whenever it prevents a collision.
Never. It confuses other drivers.

questions.explanation: Never assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way. Always yield to prevent collisions.

questions.question: A driver license is a:

options.text: Right.
Privilege.
Requirement.

questions.explanation: A driver license is a privilege, not a right. You must earn and maintain it.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an intersection. Yield to:

options.text: Oncoming vehicles also turning left.
All vehicles coming toward you.
Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting to walk.

questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to all vehicles moving toward you on a green light.

questions.question: You want to park uphill on a road with no curb. Which way should your front wheels point?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the road edge
Left, toward the road center

questions.explanation: When parking uphill or downhill on a road with no curb, turn your wheels so the car rolls away from the road center if brakes fail.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Merging traffic.
Steep hill ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns of a steep hill. Slow down to avoid collisions and brake damage.

questions.question: You are in the left lane with two lanes going your direction. Many vehicles are passing you on the right. The driver behind you wants to go faster. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in your lane to not slow down traffic.
Drive onto the left shoulder to let other vehicles pass.
Move to the right lane when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane to drive faster, pass, or turn left. Use the right lane when driving slower than other traffic, entering the road, or turning right.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection?

options.text: Yield to all traffic before crossing.
Stop, then cross when it is safe.
Slow down and cross carefully.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light tells you to slow down to a safe speed and continue with caution.

questions.question: You are on an interstate and traffic is merging from on-ramps on your right. What is the best thing to do?

options.text: Change lanes to the left.
Slow down.
Keep your speed and position the same.

questions.explanation: On interstate highways, move left when you can to let vehicles enter from the right on-ramps.

questions.question: Looking far ahead while driving on the highway:

options.text: Helps you keep up with traffic.
Reduces sudden braking or turning.
Helps you spot police officers ahead.

questions.explanation: Watch far ahead to avoid last-minute braking or turning. Looking ahead lets you be ready to stop or change lanes, drive more safely, save fuel, and keep traffic moving steady.

questions.question: In a motor vehicle on a highway, is it legal to drink alcohol?

options.text: No. It is illegal to drink from or have open alcohol containers.
Yes. It is legal if you are not the driver.
Yes. It is legal if you are driving but not drunk.

questions.correctAnswerText: No. It is illegal to drink from or have open alcohol containers.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive under the influence of alcohol. No one—driver or passenger—may drink or possess open alcohol in a vehicle while it is running.

questions.question: Your tires feel like they lost grip on the road. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down by shifting to a lower gear.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Slow down by pumping the brakes hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If your tires lose grip, ease off the gas and avoid braking. Do not try to stop or turn until your tires grip the road again.

questions.question: What do yellow lines separate?

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of roads used for two-way traffic. A solid yellow line means you cannot cross to pass. A broken yellow line means you can cross to pass if it is safe.

questions.question: What does excessive speed lead to?

options.text: It does not increase crash risk.
It improves your ability to react to danger.
It often leads to risky driving choices.

questions.correctAnswerText: It often leads to risky driving choices.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a common cause of crashes. It does not save time and often leads to risky driving choices.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Jogging trail.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign shows a crosswalk is ahead, marked or not. Watch for pedestrians and let them cross safely.

questions.question: What should you do when driving at night?

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at oncoming headlights.
Increase your distance from the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your distance from the car ahead.
questions.explanation: Increase your distance from the car ahead when it is dark. Use headlights to see better, following rules for high and low beams. Do not look at oncoming headlights to avoid glare.

questions.question: Give the right-of-way to pedestrians who are:

options.text: In a marked crosswalk.
In any crosswalk or intersection.
Crossing any street.

questions.explanation: Let pedestrians cross in marked or unmarked crosswalks. For safety, let pedestrians cross any street.

questions.question: You see a flashing yellow traffic light ahead at an intersection. What does it mean?

options.text: Stop before entering if you can do so safely.
Stop and yield to all traffic crossing.
Slow down and cross carefully.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns you to proceed with caution. Slow down and be alert. Yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles in the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Slow down and use your high beam headlights.
Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use low beams. If fog is too heavy to see through, pull off the road and wait.

questions.question: When is highway pavement most slippery?

options.text: After it has rained for several hours.
When rain first begins.
After it has rained for one to two hours.

questions.explanation: Pavement is most slippery when rain first starts. Dirt and oil on the road mix with rainwater, making a slick film.

questions.question: When is a U-turn not permitted?

options.text: In a parking lot.
On or near curves or hills.
On a straight road where you can see 500 feet both ways.

questions.correctAnswerText: On or near curves or hills.
questions.explanation: Never turn around on or near curves or hills. You cannot see oncoming traffic or pedestrians and may cause a crash.

questions.question: You are entering the interstate on a short ramp with no acceleration lane. What should you do?

options.text: Enter the right lane right away and speed up to match traffic.
Use the shoulder to speed up to match traffic.
Speed up only after you see a gap in traffic, then enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up only after you see a gap in traffic, then enter.
questions.explanation: On a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, wait for a gap in traffic, then speed up and enter. Usually, you should stay stopped while waiting for a gap.

questions.question: The best way to avoid danger while driving is to:

options.text: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
Turn off the radio.
Always keep your eyes on the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always be aware of your surroundings—in front, on the sides, and behind. Watching around you helps you see problems and change speed or position.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection with a flashing red light, what must you do?

options.text: Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go.
Slow down and go with caution.
Stop and stay stopped while the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Come to a full stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.
